speaker: Unknown

en: I don't know why he joined us, but he's one of the weird people who say, oh, it went down 30%, so I'm gonna get more equity.
zh: 我不知道他为什么还是加入了,但他是那种奇怪的人之一,会说,哦,跌了 30%,所以我能拿到更多股权。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I have more upside in this thing, I should even join quicker.
zh: 现在我在这个东西里的上行空间更大了,我应该加入得更快一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I don't know, we were lucky that he ended up joining us at that moment.
zh: 所以,我不知道,我们很幸运他最终在那一刻加入了我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was smart.
zh: 那很聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's arbitrage.
zh: 这是套利。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know you're going to make it go up.
zh: 你知道你会让它涨回去的。

en: I wasn't thinking that way, but I was in big tech.

zh: 我知道,我加入时我的定位是什么,对吧?

zh: 我看到了所有那些差距,而且当时并没有一个很好的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before training the model, you need to have the right infrastructure for it.
zh: 但在训练模型之前,你得先有合适的基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very easy.
zh: 那很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was working directly with Bazel.
zh: 我直接和 Bazel 一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did not have a lot of meetings, which, by the way, in the beginning, I was not very used to it.
zh: 我们没有很多会议,顺便说一句,一开始我不太习惯。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked Bazel to set up weekly one-on-one meeting with me, and he didn't understand what that was, because it's not a thing here in .

speaker: Unknown
en: But soon, we canceled that meeting, because we communicated with each other mostly with code, and that was much more efficient.
zh: 但很快,我们取消了那个会议,因为我们主要用代码来沟通,那效率高得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, from I guess taking it back to like when you start a business, teams are always small and you try to build something that has product market fit and scale up a company.
zh: 是的,我想说回到创办公司的时候,团队总是很小,你努力做出有产品市场契合的东西,然后把公司规模化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we started, I mean, the company was probably 10 people at the beginning and then maybe for the first three, four years, max 50 people.
zh: 我们刚开始的时候,公司一开始大概 10 个人,然后可能头三、四年,最多 50 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we always ran really lean and an advertising company.
zh: 所以我们一直以非常精简的方式运营一家广告公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can't make money, then you probably shouldn't be in business.
zh: 如果你赚不到钱,那你可能就不应该做这门生意。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但精简的文化是从一开始就有的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The types of people that we hired back then, Basel, the CTO, was the first lead engineer and then promoted the CTO four or five years later.
zh: 我们那时候招的人,Basel,CTO,是第一位首席工程师,四、五年后被提拔为 CTO。

speaker: Unknown
en: But his mindset was, I'm just going to do.
zh: 但他的心态是,我就是要去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he would just write code to solve every single problem.

speaker: Unknown
en: And up until when Geo joined,

en: Basel probably wrote, I don't know, 60% of the code of the company himself.
zh: Basel 可能亲自写了公司大概 60% 的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the mentality was always individual contributors can help us succeed in this very, very competitive field.
zh: 心态一直是,个人贡献者能帮助我们在这个竞争极其激烈的领域取得成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we never built this framework of one-on-ones and meetings and process.
zh: 所以我们从来没有建立过一对一、会议和流程这样的框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that was what appealed to Geo when he came in.
zh: 所以我想那就是 Geo 进来时吸引他的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the challenges with that style, though, is that when you don't have, like, a team constructed to actually, like, go through challenges and solve problems as a group.
zh: 不过这种风格的一个挑战是,当你没有一个真正作为团队一起去应对挑战、解决问题的团队结构时——

speaker: Unknown
en: And he can talk about, like, as we've gone over the last three years in his tenure, he's really developed that muscle.
zh: 他可以谈谈,在我们过去三年他的任期内,他真正锻炼出了那块肌肉。

speaker: Unknown
en: But my own view, just being an individual contributor myself, was always hire a bunch of great people.
zh: 但我自己的看法,我自己就是一个个人贡献者,一直是雇一堆很棒的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let them solve problems.
zh: 让他们去解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they need help, they can come to us and we'll give them help.
zh: 如果他们需要帮助,他们可以来找我们,我们会给他们帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: But otherwise, it's sort of like just off to the races.
zh: 但除此之外,基本上就是放手让他们去干。

en: And that was what Geo stepped into.

en: How big was the organization?

en: So back then we had gaming businesses too that we've since sold off.
zh: 那时候我们还有游戏业务，后来卖掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So not including those.
zh: 所以不含那部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not including Adjust, which is a software as a service company we bought, never integrated.
zh: 也不包括 Adjust，那是我们收购的一家 SaaS(软件即服务)公司，从来没有整合进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd say the company's been around 400 people for a while.
zh: 我觉得公司一段时间以来一直在 400 人左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: And about two to three years ago, we probably cut it down from 600 to 400.
zh: 大概两三年前，我们可能从 600 人裁到了 400 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we haven't really changed all that much since.
zh: 从那以后基本没有太大变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people come and go, but that's what you got.
zh: 人员有来有走，但基本就是这个规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other, I think, interesting thing for Gio when he joined was he came in and we created the Slack Room when it was Basel, Gio, and myself.
zh: 另一件我觉得对 Gio 来说很有意思的事是，他加入的时候，我们创建了那个 Slack 房间，当时就是 Basel、Gio 和我三个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we talked through the problems and it was like just real-time feedback.
zh: 我们一起讨论问题，就像实时反馈一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I don't know if him and Basel even saw Sun for those five, six months because they were just coding and racing against each other.
zh: 然后我不知道那五六个月里他和 Basel 有没有见过太阳，因为他们就是不停地写代码，互相竞赛。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the dynamic was like, okay, well, this is a new path.
zh: 但那种状态就是：好，这是一条全新的路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're effectively rebuilding the engine of the company.
zh: 所以我们实际上是在重建公司的引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't really care about what exists.
zh: 我们不太在乎已存在的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything else that has been built, the data platform, the...
zh: 其他所有已建成的，数据平台，还有那些……

speaker: Unknown
en: Software tools for developers called mediation service.
zh: 给开发者用的软件工具，叫 mediation service。

speaker: Unknown
en: All these things that we had as assets were separate, but this core engine, this algorithm, they were completely rebuilding.
zh: 所有这些我们已有的资产都是独立的，但这个核心引擎、这个算法，他们是在完全重建。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they basically went in to, I don't know where they worked out of, I know where Basel worked out of, I don't know where Geo worked out of, but
zh: 所以他们基本上就扎进去了，我不知道他们在哪儿办公，我知道 Basel 在哪儿办公，我不知道 Geo 在哪儿办公，但是

speaker: Unknown
en: They just went in and just started coding against each other and racing to get to a direction that they thought was the right place to go.
zh: 他们就是扎进去开始对着写代码，互相比赛，朝他们认为正确的方向冲刺。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was cool for me to see.
zh: 对我来说看到这一幕很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was different for Gio to see because he was used to much bigger processes around what engineers could and couldn't do with companies.
zh: 我觉得对 Gio 来说感受可能不同，因为他习惯了在大公司里工程师什么能做什么不能做的那些流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the first things I told Basel when we first started developing this company was,

speaker: Unknown
en: Technology moves really fast, and you've got to be humble about what you have and know that if technology goes faster than what you've developed, you've got to throw away what you have and re-architect it, rebuild it, and it's probably going to happen every couple years or even faster in the future.
zh: 技术迭代非常快，你必须对你已有的东西保持谦逊，并且要明白，如果技术跑得比你开发的还快，你就得扔掉手上的东西，重新做架构、重建，而且这种情况大概每几年就会发生一次，未来甚至更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was always one of the core things that we believed on engineering, is who cares about what we've built?
zh: 这一直是我们在工程上信奉的核心原则之一，就是我们建了什么有什么关系？

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's always make sure we're on something that's current or innovative or cutting edge.
zh: 我们要始终确保自己站在当下、站在创新、站在前沿的东西上。

en: So you have a lean team.
zh: 所以你有一个精简的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about 100 people on the engineering side.

en: Everybody's, quote unquote, an individual contributor.

zh: 那么，当 Axon 2 被架构的时候，当时的团队和今天非常不一样，对吧？

zh: 那些在创意上投入并且擅长的广告主，无论他们是使用 AI 工具来开发创意，还是用人来开发，都能在一个其他一切都已自动化的广告系统里创造提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: Has there been any sort of, I guess,
zh: 有没有任何一种，我想说，

speaker: Unknown
en: Has there been any sort of resolve in whether UGC is taking over traditional ads?
zh: 有没有任何关于 UGC 是否正在取代传统广告的定论？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know with, like, the proliferation of clipping, like, it's really cool, like, seeing on social media, I put out content every day.
zh: 我知道，比如，随着剪辑（clipping）的普及，这真的很酷，比如在社交媒体上看到，我每天都发布内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I put out content before where, like, there was this, like, prebiotic, probiotic...
zh: 而我之前发布过一条内容，关于一种……益生元益生菌……

speaker: Unknown
en: Like bar, I bought it, I ate it.
zh: 比如那种棒状零食，我买了，我吃了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, oh my gosh, this is like Ozempic.
zh: 我当时想，天哪，这就像 Ozempic。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I tweeted that.
zh: 然后我发推说了这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: They made that tweet an ad and it became like a Forex ROI ad for them.
zh: 他们把那条推文做成了广告，结果成了他们一个投资回报率超高的广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they just like made so much money on it.
zh: 然后他们靠它赚了好多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got no money.
zh: 我一分钱都没拿到。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like, but like there are like different kinds of things that have made more ads more effective than others in this proliferation of UGC and what looks like clipping and what looks like just normal social feed has kind of risen.
zh: 但是，比如在这种 UGC 的普及中，有些东西确实让某些广告比其他的更有效，而看起来像剪辑、像普通社交信息流的东西已经兴起了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you seen anything with that?
zh: 你有看到这方面的情况吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, some advertisers can make that work on us because there's a wide range of things that work, but I'd say social is really high ADD, so everyone wants to get to the point really quickly.
zh: 我是说，有些广告主可以在我们平台上把这一套玩得转，因为能奏效的东西范围很广，但我得说社交媒体的注意力非常涣散（高 ADD），所以每个人都想非常快地进入正题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Typically, like a social ad will say, you got three seconds to capture attention, that's it, and otherwise you lost the user.
zh: 通常，比如一条社交广告会说，你有三秒钟去抓住注意力，仅此而已，否则你就失去了这个用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our world where the user's sitting and engaging with the ad for such a longer extended timeframe and the user is just frankly different, the person who's playing a solitaire or mahjong is not the power user scrolling on Instagram and TikTok all day long.
zh: 而在我们的世界里，用户参与广告的时间要长得多，而且说实话用户也完全不同，玩纸牌或麻将的人，不是那个整天刷 Instagram 和 TikTok 的高级用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you've got a different person, probably the power user's older.
zh: 所以你面对的是不同的人，高级用户可能年纪更大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their mind is not working in the same way as someone who's grown up in today's culture.
zh: 他们大脑的运作方式和在当今文化中长大的人不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have smarter people?
zh: 所以他们是比较聪明的人？

speaker: Unknown
en: I wouldn't call them smarter, differently constructed minds.
zh: 我不会说他们更聪明，是构造方式不同的大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is alpha in this.
zh: 这里面是有超额收益（alpha）的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're just wired differently.
zh: 他们的接线方式就是不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is part of the education process.
zh: 这是教育过程的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: In gaming, we've been in the space 12 years.
zh: 在游戏领域，我们在这个空间已经 12 年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The game customers really brought to market playables that are the minigame preview in the ad, I want to say like 10 years ago.
zh: 游戏客户真正把试玩广告（playable）——就是广告里的那种小游戏预览——推向市场，我想说大概是在 10 年前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the ad stayed pretty consistent since then because it's just a really good ad.
zh: 而且从那以后这种广告形式一直相当稳定，因为它就是一条非常好的广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get the minigame and then you get the download behind.
zh: 你先玩到小游戏，然后后面就是下载。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got into this consumer vertical and more specifically e-commerce 18 months ago, roughly.
zh: 我们进入这个消费垂直领域，更具体地说是电商，大约是 18 个月前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're so early in a market, you have to educate the market on what works.
zh: 所以你在一个市场里非常早期，你必须教育这个市场什么才是有效的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that where alpha comes to play here is some of the customers who go, I'm gonna invest in this platform early on.
zh: 而这里超额收益（alpha）发挥作用的地方，就是那些说“我要尽早投资这个平台”的客户，

speaker: Unknown
en: And really learn how the users behave, who the users are and what they're willing to buy and what kind of ads to build, create alpha.
zh: 真正去学习用户如何行为、用户是谁、他们愿意买什么、以及该做什么样的广告，从而创造超额收益（alpha）。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get to create much larger campaigns and successful metrics on us than those who come in and just go, look, I'm going to run the same UGC ad I do on social over here.
zh: 他们在我们平台上能创建规模大得多的广告活动，并取得比那些进来就说“听着，我要把我在社交平台上跑的同一条 UGC 广告直接搬到这边来跑”的人好得多的指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we don't have three seconds.
zh: 可是，我们没有那三秒钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: They had a lot longer to actually go engage the user and have that user remember their brand, but they chose not to take that.
zh: 他们其实有长得多的时间去真正让用户参与、让用户记住他们的品牌，但他们选择了不这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll take time for us to make sure agencies and advertisers understand these concepts, but it does create a world where early on in a platform advertisers who are paying attention get alpha.
zh: 让广告代理机构和广告主理解这些概念需要时间，但这确实造成了一个局面：在一个平台的早期，用心关注的广告主能获得超额收益（alpha）。

speaker: Unknown
en: How has AI changed the making of ads?
zh: AI 如何改变了广告的制作？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's early.
zh: 现在还很早。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like you can get a good clip, a short ad out of some of the large language models.
zh: 现在还不像你能从某些大语言模型那里直接得到一条好的短片、一条短广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: The challenge is to get them to put together a 30 to 60 second video advertisement for a brand that doesn't mess anything up because you can't like anything wrong in that video, the brand is not going to approve it to run.
zh: 挑战在于让它们为一个品牌拼出一条 30 到 60 秒的视频广告，而且不搞砸任何东西，因为那条视频里不能有任何错误，品牌是不会批准它投放的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so can't mess anything up, have to be engaging, and for a pretty long extended time frame, not that easy yet.
zh: 所以不能搞砸任何东西，还得有吸引力，而且要在相当长的时间跨度内保持，这目前还没那么容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not at a place where you're just going to get a massive amount of inflow of advertisements that are diverse and creatively inspired and going to create lifts and campaigns.
zh: 所以它还没到那个地步——你还不能获得大量多样化的、有创意启发的广告流入，并由此带来广告活动的提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: But their tools are available now so that humans can create ads much faster and much lower cost.
zh: 但他们的工具现在已经可用，所以人类可以更快、成本更低地创作广告。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've seen much more ad content coming into the system.
zh: 所以我们看到越来越多广告内容进入系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just not at a point where the average marketer can go type into a box and say, here's a great ad, and off we go.
zh: 只是还没到那种程度，让普通营销人员可以往一个框里输入，然后说，这是一条很棒的广告，我们开工吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: From our product, we saw a lot of AI-assisted content on the platform by advertisers.
zh: 从我们的产品来看，我们看到平台上有很多广告主使用 AI 辅助创作的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, you know, it's important to still have the human in the loop to guardrail the process because advertisement is about trust.
zh: 我认为，你知道，仍然要让人类保持在流程中以护栏这个过程，这很重要，因为广告关乎信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you create a content that breaks the brand image and it will break the trust and it's harder to convince users to buy.
zh: 如果你创作的内容破坏了品牌形象，就会破坏信任，也就更难说服用户购买。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, so there are two different types in terms of the AI generated as content.
zh: 但是，所以 AI 生成内容方面有两种不同的类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are two different approaches.
zh: 有两种不同的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can try to approach it.
zh: 你可以尝试切入。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is you make this tool entirely automatic, right?
zh: 一种是把这个工具做成完全自动化的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what, if AppLoving is building such a product, this is what we aim because we're not serving one single advertiser.
zh: 这就是，如果 AppLoving 要打造这样一款产品，这就是我们的目标，因为我们服务的不是单一的广告主。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're serving all the advertisers.
zh: 我们服务的是所有广告主。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to create a tool that can fully automate everything.
zh: 我们必须打造一个能把一切完全自动化的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other choice is you just create a tool that allows advertisers to interact with, to allow them to collaborate with the AI tool to create their own content.
zh: 另一种选择是你只做一个供广告主交互的工具，让他们与 AI 工具协作来创作自己的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: So right now we see that the second type of tools has been pretty widely adopted, but I think there's still more challenges for the first approach and we're still working on that.
zh: 所以目前我们看到第二种类型的工具已经被相当广泛地采用，但我认为第一种方法仍然面临更多挑战，我们也还在努力中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you guys thought about buying any of these kinds of companies?
zh: 你们有没有考虑过收购这类公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a company called Higgsfield.
zh: 有一家叫 Higgsfield 的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like, I mean, how do you scope out R&D on this kind of like new market that's opening up?
zh: 就是说，你们如何针对这种正在打开的新市场来规划研发？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it is much easier to get content that is short.
zh: 我是说，获取较短的内容要容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're optimized for social and UGC, which these things, if you want to create a 10-second clip and put it on TikTok or Instagram, you can do it out of the box.
zh: 所以这些工具是为社交和 UGC 优化的，如果你想创作一段 10 秒的短片放到 TikTok 或 Instagram 上，你可以开箱即用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Higgsfield is a tool for influencers.
zh: 而 Higgsfield 是一个面向网红的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not the advertiser on the other side of our product.
zh: 那不是我们产品另一端的广告主。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you get a brand as big as a Wayfair and you hand them something out of the box that looks not ideal for their brand, they lose trust in you as a platform.
zh: 如果你面对的是像 Wayfair 这样大的品牌，而你交给他们一个开箱即用、看起来并不适合他们品牌的东西，他们就会对你这个平台失去信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: And certainly you can't run that on their behalf.
zh: 而且你肯定不能代表他们去投放那样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they got to get something that is compelling enough for their brand to be as good as what a human builds and maintain brand trust and have extended time in it.
zh: 所以他们必须得到对其品牌足够有吸引力的东西，要和人类创作的一样好，维护品牌信任，并且有更长的时长。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's nothing in the market that we've seen that solves that problem.
zh: 所以我们在市场上还没有看到能解决这个问题的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Generally, when we see these problems,
zh: 一般来说，当我们遇到这些问题时，

speaker: Unknown
en: that are hard to solve and specific more to us than just the general market, our team has to develop too.
zh: 那些难以解决、相比一般市场对我们来说更特定的问题，我们的团队也得自己开发。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so we covered a lot internally to kind of take it a little bit back into macro.
zh: 正如我们之前分享的，工程团队的规模和今天基本一样，和三年前一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of people are trying to rebuild right now for the AI era.
zh: 很多人现在都在尝试为 AI 时代进行重构。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've listened to many of, Adam, your interviews where you're talking about you build for the next, you know, three, four or five years along ahead of you.
zh: 我听过很多 Adam 你的访谈，你谈到你要为你前面接下来三、四或五年而构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: So whatever you built right now, you know, you built back in 2022, 2023 or so.
zh: 所以你现在构建的东西，你知道，是你大约在 2022、2023 年的时候构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious, does that still hold?
zh: 我很好奇，这个说法现在还成立吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you rebuild in such an era where things move so fast?
zh: 在这样一个变化如此之快的时代，你们如何重构？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I don't really want to rebuild.
zh: 是的，我其实并不想重构。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the last three years, we've built a lot of things that made us feel so proud of.
zh: 在过去三年里，我们构建了很多让我们非常自豪的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is powerful, but I don't think that's a reason for us to rebuild.
zh: AI 很强大，但我不认为那是我们重构的理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: What AI really helps us to do is to build on top of what we have today.
zh: AI 真正帮助我们做的，是在我们今天已有的东西之上进行构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: With the empowerment of AI, we were able to achieve much more.
zh: 有了 AI 的赋能，我们能够实现更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have been thinking about this growth trajectory, this growth journey of our company.
zh: 我一直在思考我们公司的这条增长轨迹、这段增长历程。

speaker: Unknown
en: As we shared previously, the size of the engineering team was basically the same size as today as three years ago.
zh: 正如我们之前分享过的，工程团队的规模和三年前基本一样大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And typically when a company went through such a growth of their business, you know, your scale of your business is much larger.
zh: 通常当一家公司经历了这样的业务增长时，你知道，你的业务规模会大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The type of problems you're solving is also much more sophisticated.
zh: 你要解决的问题类型也会复杂得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this kind of growth has to be paired with the growth of headcount and team size.
zh: 而这种增长必须与人数和团队规模的增长相匹配。

speaker: Unknown
en: But luckily, you know, I feel our growth just was perfectly in sync with the advancement of AI.
zh: 但幸运的是，你知道，我觉得我们的增长正好与 AI 的进步完美同步。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as the problem we are solving becomes more complicated and our team was elevated by AI, so we were able to manage the same size of the team while we're solving more challenging problems.
zh: 所以随着我们解决的问题变得更复杂，而我们的团队被 AI 提升了，所以我们能够在保持团队规模不变的同时解决更具挑战性的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: As we're speaking now, you know,
zh: 就像我们现在交谈的同时，你知道，

speaker: Unknown
en: We built this model, the new generation model three years ago.
zh: 我们在三年前构建了这个模型，新一代模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now with the assistance of AI, the team was able to tackle and work on a new generation model that would be even more powerful.
zh: 现在在 AI 的辅助下，团队能够攻克并研发一个会更加强大的新一代模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So back to your question.
zh: 回到你之前的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think we need to rebuild anything, but we are definitely building on top of what we have today.
zh: 我不认为我们需要重建什么，但我们确实是在今天已有的东西之上进行构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the business side, we keep the team really lean as well.
zh: 在业务方面，我们也保持团队非常精简。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you wouldn't be able to scale out the products we want to scale out with the team sizes that we target in the past.
zh: 如果按照我们过去的团队规模，你是不可能把我们想要扩张的产品都扩张出去的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if we can get to a place where eventually everyone on the business team is doing something and then ask the question, could this be automated and done across the whole advertiser base?
zh: 但如果我们能做到这一点——最终业务团队里的每个人都在做某件事，然后提出这样一个问题：这件事能不能被自动化并在整个广告主群体中推广？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they actually understood how to use AI or they go to, we have central folks and a team that actually can create tools, dashboards and automation for them, can go take that process and then automate it.
zh: 而且他们真正懂得如何使用 AI，或者说他们去找——我们有中心化的人员和一个团队，能真正为他们创建工具、仪表盘和自动化，然后把这个流程拿去自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll get to a place a couple of years from now where hopefully most every process is automated and
zh: 几年之后，我们会到达一个阶段，希望那时几乎所有流程都被自动化了，而且

speaker: Unknown
en: Then the business interpersonal skills matter a lot.
zh: 到那时，业务上的人际交往能力就变得非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not going to be able to replace sitting down with the customer at a QBR and understanding their business because our AI as an enterprise can understand our business.
zh: 你不可能取代与客户坐下来开 QBR、了解他们业务这件事，因为我们的 AI 作为企业只能理解我们自己的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can't understand the businesses of advertisers.
zh: 它无法理解广告主们的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we always say our job is to be their growth consultant.
zh: 所以我们总是说，我们的工作是成为他们的增长顾问。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's to understand what their needs are.
zh: 是去了解他们的需求是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then deliver value that meets their needs on our platform.
zh: 然后在我们的平台上交付能满足他们需求的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a lot of the interpersonal relationship skills there that the AI can't replace.
zh: 所以这里面有很多 AI 无法取代的人际关系技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we want to get to is a place where the team is scalable, most of the processes are automated, and then those people are really sitting down with the customer, making a difference in building relationships.
zh: 我们想要达到的状态是：团队是可扩展的，大部分流程都被自动化了，然后这些人真正与客户坐下来，在建立关系方面发挥作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I guess most people are trying to rebuild right now because they're acting a little bit more reactively versus proactively is what I was trying to get at.
zh: 所以我想，现在大多数人都在试图重建，是因为他们的应对方式更像是在被动反应，而不是主动规划，这就是我想表达的意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in terms of others that are trying to rebuild right now, what do you think the biggest mistakes that they'll make are?
zh: 那么对于其他正在试图重建的公司，你认为他们会犯的最大错误是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a very interesting question.
zh: 这是一个非常有意思的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think everyone here would agree.
zh: 我想在座每个人都会同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: The AI is helping us to improve the productivity of every engineer, every business person tremendously.
zh: AI 正在帮助每一位工程师、每一位业务人员极大地提升生产力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's also kind of interesting to see that not every company, not every organization has been able to multiply their output as a result of the AI empowerment.
zh: 但同样很有意思的是，并不是每家公司、每个组织都能凭借 AI 赋能实现产出的倍增。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a big, big mistake that people are making is that because of the AI, building things become easier.
zh: 我认为人们正在犯的一个很大的、很大的错误是：因为 AI 让构建东西变得更容易了。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are making a lot of bad decisions, bad tastes, wasteful ideas that actually offset the empowerment of AI.
zh: 人们做出了很多糟糕的决策、糟糕的品味、浪费的想法，这些实际上抵消了 AI 带来的赋能。

speaker: Unknown
en: You build things faster, but you're making a lot of bad-tasted ideas.

en: And we like to think just in traditional finance terms, you're worth your cash flow after SBC and what you expect that to be many years out into the future and the terminal value of it.

zh: 嗯，游戏品类我们做得非常好。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以因此，你要进入消费端，你才能真正提升你能获取的资金规模以及你能服务的公司范围。

zh: 仅凭这一点，大概在较短的时间期限内——再说明一次，我说较短指的是五年以上——也无法让我们到达那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then you have to start thinking about, okay, what else beyond that?
zh: 所以你就得开始思考，好吧，除此之外还有什么？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 并且在那里执行得极其出色，从而达到了那个目标。

zh: 所以我认为，作为业务上的伙伴，我和 Gio 的职责就是去思考，在未来的五到十年里，除了执行好我们的核心业务之外，我们还要做哪些其他的事情？

zh: 所以当我们构建系统的时候，比如数据基础设施，对吧，我们就必须去预想，为了支撑一家价值万亿美元的公司，我们在设计时必须把什么样的规模因素考虑进去？

zh: 如果你有一个围绕它的计划，或者人们有信心你能朝那个方向引领，你最终就能到达那里。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 太棒了。

zh: 所以我们总是以固定美元的角度来考虑这件事,我们想要给员工非常优厚的报酬,但我们不想过度支付,而且我们保持精简的团队。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以这始终是可控的。

zh: 而在另一面,我们产生了大量现金。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以当股价暴跌时,我们不需要去说,瞧,我们得去说服投资者来买这只股票。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以我们能够反过来做,说,我们就要买自己的股票。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而在另一面,我们要把赚到的每一美元甚至更多都投进去,开始回购我们自己的股票,做我们自己最好的投资者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it is company specific and some of these companies will have a tough time recovering.
zh: 所以这是因公司而异的,其中一些公司将很难恢复。

zh: 你认为它们会发生什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of times when companies reach that point where it's tough and revenue multiple and potential cashflow multiple, if you do big layoffs, it ends up pretty low, they start getting accumulated by private equity or effectively plucked off the public markets, taken private, because the only way to recover it is a complete restructure.
zh: 很多时候,当公司到了那个艰难的境地,收入倍数和潜在的现金流倍数,如果你进行大规模裁员的话,最终会变得相当低,它们开始被私募股权收购,或者实际上被从公开市场摘除、私有化,因为恢复的唯一办法就是彻底的重组。

speaker: Unknown
en: You fire a lot of people, you cashflow it, you lever the business up, and that fits the private equity model.
zh: 你解雇很多人,你的现金流,你给业务加杠杆,而那符合私募股权的模式。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你最兴奋的是什么?

en: The team is constantly making changes to the models.

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think Apploving is different.

en: So every individual in the company just has the outsize of growth.

zh: 而且我觉得,看到公司成长,看到我自己成长,看到团队里的人学到更多、变得更加成熟,这让我保持兴奋。

en: I don't get excited.

en: And so I never think of the world in excitement terms.

zh: 所以我只是学会了把这两种情绪都管理掉，真正努力去想，好，让我们确保这里有合适的人和合适的路径，然后其他一切都会水到渠成。

zh: 我就想尽一切努力让它实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you think most people don't do that?
zh: 你为什么觉得大多数人不会这样做？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, maybe it's a type of vitamin I add since I was young.
zh: 我不知道，也许这是我从年轻时就添加的一种维生素。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, just like personality thing.
zh: 它的坏处是，很难达到满足感或幸福感，或者很多其他人会有的那些情绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that become an obstacle sometimes?
zh: 这有时会成为障碍吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be, yeah.
zh: 可能会，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes I feel like it becomes an obstacle because I had a hard time to pause and enjoy the achievement we have.
zh: 有时我觉得它成为障碍，因为我很难停下来享受我们已经取得的成就。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I don't know if Adam feels the same thing.
zh: 比如，我不知道 Adam 是否也有同样的感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was, you know, a lot of excitement in the past because of the success of Apple Living, but I just find myself hard to take, like, press the pause button and just enjoy that moment.
zh: 你知道，过去因为 Apple Living 的成功有很多兴奋，但我发现自己很难按下暂停键，去享受那一刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we do have a trillion dollar milestone half of us.
zh: 嗯，我们确实有一个万亿美元里程碑的一半。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think then you have the next one.
zh: 我想然后你会有下一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is actually a common trait I've found in really highly competent, successful people is like there is no moment to really enjoy because there's no sort of goal that you get to once you get to one you're on to the next one.
zh: 这其实是我在真正非常有能力、成功的人身上发现的一个共同特质，就是没有真正可以享受的时刻，因为没有任何一个你到达后就结束的目标，一旦你到达一个，你就开始奔向下一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's sort of like, I mean, when you're raised in households where like the A is not good enough, you got to get the A plus, a lot of times that builds this in people.
zh: 这有点像，我是说，当你成长在这样的家庭——A 还不够好，你必须拿到 A 加——很多时候这会在人身上培养出这种特质。

speaker: Unknown
en: The downside of it is it's hard to reach fulfillment or happiness or some of the emotions like a lot of others would have.
zh: 它的坏处是,很难达到满足感或幸福感,或者其他很多人所能拥有的那些情绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you're always achieving for more, you're pushing yourself to keep going and no moment is good enough.
zh: 但如果你总是在追求更多，你就在推动自己不断前进，没有任何时刻是足够好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there any other traits you look for?
zh: 还有其他你看重的特质吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Any players?
zh: 任何的特质？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the type of people I really like in my team, they usually have two characters.
zh: 我觉得我在团队里真正喜欢的人，通常有两个特质。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one is intelligence.
zh: 一个是智力。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second is having low ego.
zh: 第二是低自我。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the intelligence part is easy to understand.
zh: 我认为智力这部分很好理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has to be smart.
zh: 必须聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learns fast, you know, has higher standard for themselves, get things done, right?
zh: 学得快，你知道，对自己有更高的标准，把事情做完，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is, I think, the character a lot of companies are looking at.
zh: 我认为这是很多公司都在看的那种特质。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think the second part, having low ego, is often overlooked.
zh: 但我认为第二部分，低自我，经常被忽视。

speaker: Unknown
en: When a person has low ego, he tends to listen, he tends to empower his team, tends to help others, and more importantly, they take feedbacks.
zh: 当一个人有低自我时，他倾向于倾听，倾向于赋能他的团队，倾向于帮助别人，更重要的是，他们接受反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they proactively question themselves.
zh: 然后他们会主动地质疑自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a very important part for growth.
zh: 这是成长中非常重要的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it usually helps with the third thing which I look for and always ask about is how they react to adversity.
zh: 而且它通常有助于第三件我看重并且总是问的事情，就是他们如何应对逆境。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing is easy in the world and some people grew up with easier upbringings than other people and usually people who know how to respond well to adversity do really well.
zh: 世界上没有什么是容易的，有些人成长环境比别人容易，而通常懂得如何很好应对逆境的人会做得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a kind of like a danger for high performers because when you're a high performer, a lot of people around you, they observe you as a high performer.
zh: 这对高绩效者来说是一种类似危险的东西，因为当你是高绩效者时，你周围很多人会把你视为高绩效者。

speaker: Unknown
en: They trust you.
zh: 他们信任你。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't question you, right?
zh: 他们不质疑你，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it becomes extremely important for those high performers to be able to question themselves.
zh: 所以对于那些高绩效者来说，能够质疑自己就变得极其重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've seen, you know, some people did extremely well in this, but some others might forget to be the one that challenges themselves.
zh: 我见过，你知道，有些人在这方面做得非常好，但另一些人可能忘了成为挑战自己的那一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know I said I already asked a difficult question, and I almost left out without asking this one, but Adam, okay, you built out a gaming advertising company.
zh: 我知道我说过我已经问了一个难题，而且我差点没问这个问题就结束了，但 Adam，好的，你建立了一家游戏广告公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're in the gaming space.
zh: 你在游戏领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know who else was in the gaming space?
zh: 你知道还有谁在游戏领域吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, we had Torsten, who then went on to found Helsing.
zh: 好的，我们有 Torsten，他后来创立了 Helsing。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had Palmer Luckey, who went on to found Andurl.
zh: 我们有 Palmer Luckey，他后来创立了 Andurl。

speaker: Unknown
en: What comes after AppLovin for you?
zh: AppLovin 之后，对你来说会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a tough question.
zh: 这是个难题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm probably, hopefully, if I'm good enough and earn people's trust around me, I'm going to be the CEO for a long time.
zh: 我可能会——希望——如果我足够优秀并且赢得周围人的信任，我会长期担任 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I don't think about the after at this point as a public company's CEO running a business this large.
zh: 所以在这一点上，作为一家上市公司的 CEO，经营着如此大规模的业务，我不去想以后的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it changed for me along the way because I'll say when we were smaller, I did used to think about building again.
zh: 我认为这一路走来这对我发生了变化，因为我要说，当我们还比较小的时候，我确实曾经想过再次创业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I do really love the early stage.
zh: 而且我真的很喜欢早期阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not a lot of people in the world have gotten the privilege to be able to work with people and together build something from zero to a hundred billion dollars plus.
zh: 世界上没有很多人有幸能够与他人一起从零打造出价值一千亿美元以上的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so where we are, we've just got so much opportunity in front of us, I can't really sit there thinking about what's after this.
zh: 所以我们现在面前有这么多机会，我真的没法坐在那里去想这之后的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, that's a great place to end.
zh: 哇，这是个很好的收尾。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Gio, Adam, this was such an interesting and different and thoughtful conversation.
zh: 好了，Gio、Adam，这是一次非常有趣、与众不同且发人深省的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for giving a deep dive inside the engineering side of AppLovin and the growth that you guys have achieved.
zh: 非常感谢你们深入剖析了 AppLovin 工程方面的内幕以及你们所取得的增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really appreciate it.
zh: 我真的很感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks again for having us.
zh: 再次感谢你们的邀请。
